aciklama: 1,500-year-old domed landmark with Byzantine and Ottoman heritage. Tourists visit the upper gallery via a separate entrance; the ground floor is open for worship. Queues can be long.
Mosque famous for its İznik tiles, free to visit. Modest clothing is required and shoes must be removed. The courtyard is wide and flat.
Palace of the Ottoman sultans. Large courtyards, the Harem, the treasury and terraces with Bosphorus views. A full visit takes 3-4 hours, with a lot of walking and some stairs.
Underground Byzantine cistern; dim lighting, walkways above the water and the Medusa heads. A long staircase leads down at the entrance; inside it is cool and damp.
Thousands of ancient artifacts including the Alexander Sarcophagus. Next to Gülhane Park, quiet and away from the crowds. Some halls may be under restoration.
Historic covered bazaar with more than 4,000 shops: carpets, jewelry, ceramics, leather. Very crowded, narrow corridors, bargaining culture. Slight slopes at the entrances.
Historic bazaar selling spices, Turkish delight, nuts and coffee. Colorful and fragrant, very crowded at weekends. The floor is flat, but moving around can be hard due to the crowds.
Mimar Sinan's masterpiece. Golden Horn views from its garden, a quiet and peaceful atmosphere. The streets leading up the hill are steep.
Medieval stone tower with a 360-degree city view from the narrow balcony at the top. There is an elevator, but the last floors are climbed by stairs. Long queues at sunset.
Magnificent 19th-century palace on the Bosphorus; a giant crystal chandelier and the room where Atatürk died. Guided tours only, no photography inside. Its gardens are flat and well kept.
Some of the best-preserved Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world. A small, cramped building; the neighborhood streets are cobblestone.
Transport and industry museum on the Golden Horn: a submarine, planes, trains, classic cars. Exhibits you can touch and climb into, large flat areas, a cafe and a restaurant.
Modern and contemporary Turkish art in a building designed by Renzo Piano. Has elevators, fully accessible, and a restaurant with a waterfront terrace.
Osman Hamdi Bey's The Tortoise Trainer and changing international exhibitions. Has elevators; a mid-sized, quiet museum.
A small, poetic museum born from Orhan Pamuk's novel. An old house with narrow, steep stairs; a quiet and personal experience.
Carpet, calligraphy and ethnography collection in İbrahim Pasha Palace. Stairs at the entrance; not crowded.
Bosphorus fortress built by Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror. Steep stone stairs without railings lead up to the walls; great Bosphorus views.
Elegant summer palace on the Asian shore of the Bosphorus. Calmer than Dolmabahçe; its garden has a waterfront tea garden.
Legendary tower on a small islet in the Bosphorus, reached by boat. The sunset and city views are very romantic. There are steps at the pier and on the boat.
One of the city's highest hills: a large park and viewing terrace overlooking both continents. Tea gardens, lawns, and you can drive up to the top.
Historic coffeehouse and viewpoint overlooking the Golden Horn. Reached by cable car, or on foot through a cemetery. Tea and coffee are affordable.
One of Istanbul's most sacred pilgrimage sites. Very crowded especially on Fridays and religious holidays; a deeply spiritual atmosphere.
acilis_saatleri: All day, visits restricted during prayer times

aciklama: Open-air park with miniature models of Turkey's landmarks. Flat walking paths, a children's playground and a small train.
Thousands of sea creatures in themed sections plus a rainforest section. Fully indoors with a flat route, stroller-friendly. Far from the city center.
Aquarium with a glass shark tunnel inside Forum mall. Being inside the mall, it has elevators and is easily accessible.
Indoor LEGO play center for children aged 3-10: 4D cinema, mini rides, building areas. Adults are not allowed without children.
Large grove overlooking the Bosphorus; tulip festival in April, historic pavilions, ponds and picnic areas. Some paths are sloped; good for walking a dog.
Large wooded park that was once a palace garden; cafes in the Malta and Çadır pavilions. Hilly paths, shady and cool.
The outer garden of Topkapı Palace; ideal for resting in the tourist area. Wide flat paths, benches and a tea garden overlooking the Bosphorus.
The city's green lung; 6-8 km walking and running trails around the reservoirs, cycling, picnics. Dirt paths, hard to reach by public transport.
Green valley park between Nişantaşı and Beşiktaş. Full of dog walkers and runners; a cable car line passes over it.
Seaside park where young people sit on the grass at sunset and dogs run around. Flat promenade, affordable cafes and ice cream shops nearby.
Kilometers-long flat seaside promenade: cycling and walking lanes, playgrounds, lawns. Very suitable for families and dog owners.
Historic Polish village in the forest. Village breakfast, nature walks, horse riding and ATV tours. Requires a private car to get there.
The largest island with no motor vehicles: mansions, cycling, electric vehicle tours, a steep walk up to Aya Yorgi hill, fish restaurants. 1.5 hours by ferry.
Calmer than Büyükada, an island with pine forests. Walking, cycling and swimming in small coves. Some roads are hilly.
Long sandy beach on the Black Sea. Beach clubs in summer, rough sea and surfing. One hour from the city.
Sandy beach where a river meets the sea; kayaking, ATV, horse riding and camping. A wild, untouched feel with limited facilities.
Scientific garden with thousands of tree species and ponds. Silence rule: picnics, bicycles and pets are not allowed. Beautiful for photographers in autumn.
Terraced grove overlooking the Bosphorus; a cafe under the trees, quiet lawns. The entrances are sloped.
Baroque mosque and busy pier square right under the Bosphorus Bridge. Baked potato and waffle stalls, handmade jewelry stands, lively in the evenings.
1.4 km pedestrian street from Taksim to Tünel; nostalgic tram, arcades, street musicians. Very crowded day and night.
Lively local market full of fishmongers, pickle shops, delis and meyhanes. Ideal for seeing local life and snacking; narrow and crowded streets.
Historic Greek and Jewish neighborhood with colorful houses, antique shops and cafes. Very popular for photos; steep slopes and cobblestone streets.
Bosphorus shore lined with wooden mansions; quiet walks, strawberry ice cream and fish restaurants.
Upscale neighborhood with chic cafes and a Bosphorus promenade. The flat waterfront between Bebek and Rumeli Hisarı is loved by runners and dog owners.
Modern mall with luxury stores, a performing arts center and restaurants. Fully accessible, with baby rooms and parking.
Large mall with open-air and indoor sections; gourmet market, children's play areas, cinema. Elevators and ramps, and a pet-friendly policy.
Small, calm and orderly bazaar behind the Blue Mosque. Carpets, ceramics and textiles; less tiring than the Grand Bazaar.
Street lined with international luxury brands; chic cafes and boutiques. Sidewalks are wide and flat.
Legendary restaurant serving forgotten regional dishes from across Anatolia. You fill your plate at the counter; the menu changes daily. Small and crowded.
Historic Ottoman restaurant with turquoise tiles above the entrance of the Spice Bazaar. Famous for its eggplant börek. Reached by a narrow, steep staircase.
Kebab restaurant famous for its terrace overlooking the Golden Horn. Pistachio kebab and lahmacun; suitable for large groups and families, has an elevator.
Since 1920: a single type of meatball, bean salad and semolina halva. Fast service, simple setting, affordable.
Chic tradesmen's restaurant with turquoise tiles; home-style dishes at lunch, meze and rakı in the evening. Also popular for business lunches; reservation recommended.
Award-winning fine dining restaurant on a hotel rooftop with 360-degree views. New Anatolian cuisine tasting menu, smart dress, calm and romantic.
Innovative Turkish cuisine with Golden Horn views in the SALT Galata building. Tasting menu, wine pairing, reservation required.
International cuisine and sushi on a large terrace overlooking the Bosphorus at the top of Ulus Park. Romantic at sunset; a favorite for business dinners.
Classic fish restaurant serving in an old wooden house and its garden. Seasonal fish and meze; pleasant under the trees in the evening.
Long-established fish and meze restaurant in the northern Bosphorus, open for decades. Quiet, quality service; for special dinners.
Southeastern Turkish cuisine since 1912; çiğ köfte, kebabs and künefe. Large dining rooms, good for big family meals.
Ocakbaşı grill where the master cooks over charcoal in front of you. Friendly, noisy and smoky; queues in the evening.
Historic shop serving boza with cinnamon and roasted chickpeas since 1876. Small, you drink it standing up; a nostalgic stop.
Baklava, Turkish delight, milk puddings and Turkish coffee. Seating upstairs; a dessert break for all ages.
Istanbul's most famous baklava shop; pistachio baklava and su böreği. Crowded, fast service, ideal for a short break.
Nostalgic patisserie from 1923; famous for its Kup Griye ice cream sundae. A quiet garden at the back.
Tiny coffee shop with small stools on a side street off İstiklal, famous for its thick, foamy Turkish coffee. People sit side by side and conversations start easily.
Specialty coffee roaster; filter coffee and espresso. Many people work on laptops or come alone; dogs are welcome.
Tea and breakfast under a centuries-old plane tree right by the sea. Affordable, flat ground, peaceful Bosphorus view.
Village breakfast and milk desserts on the Bosphorus shore. Crowded at weekends; large tables and a garden for families.
Rich Van-style breakfast: herbed cheese, murtuğa, clotted cream and honey. Queues at weekends; the place is narrow, with stairs.
Pedestrian street lined with breakfast places; popular with students and young people, lively and noisy.
Giant baked potatoes filled with toppings of your choice. Eaten standing or by the water; a favorite of kids and young people.
Grilled mackerel sandwiches from rocking, decorated boats, with pickle juice on the side. Eaten on low stools on the shore; crowded and touristy.
Stalls with stuffed mussels, kokoreç, lakerda and fresh fish. An essential stop on food tours; loud and colorful.
Restaurant reviving 500-year-old Ottoman recipes from the palace kitchen archives. Unique for history lovers; calm and elegant.
Ottoman palace dishes in Sultanahmet; lamb shank, hünkar beğendi. Tourist-friendly, multilingual menu.
Modern Ottoman cuisine in a historic police station building right on the Bosphorus. Candlelit waterfront tables; for special nights.
Chic restaurant and nightclub on a hill overlooking the Bosphorus. Dress code; for corporate events and luxury evenings.
Bebek's popular cafe-bar; brunch by day, cocktails in the evening. Crowded and social, sidewalk tables.
Restaurant-bar with 360-degree views on the rooftop of a historic building on İstiklal. Turns into a club with DJ sets at weekends.
Small, intimate jazz club near Galata Tower. Live jazz every night; dim lighting, seated layout, reservation recommended.
Street full of affordable bars, the meeting point of students and young people. Crowded until late at night, music and chatting in the street.
Alternative bar and concert venue with a back garden; independent music and DJ nights. Relaxed, a place where young people and solo visitors mix easily.
Coworking space next to the business district, rentable by the day; meeting rooms, fast internet, coffee. Close to the metro.
Historic hammam built by Mimar Sinan in 1584; scrub and foam massage. Separate sections for women and men; the floor is slippery and hot.
Restored luxury Sinan hammam; calm, well kept, by appointment. Special packages for couples.
One of the last great Ottoman hammams, from 1741; a marble interior featured in film scenes. Stairs at the entrance.
Sema (whirling dervish) ceremony and Turkish dance shows in a restored hammam. About 1 hour; silence and respect are expected.
Long Bosphorus tour to Anadolu Kavağı by municipal ferry (1.5 hours one way). Affordable, open deck, seagulls. Boarding via a ramp.
2-hour sunset tour on a yacht, small-group or private charter; drinks and meze served. For couples and special celebrations.
Turkey's largest theme park with roller coasters, water rides and kids' areas. High-speed coasters for thrill seekers, a separate area for little ones.
Mini city where children aged 4-14 try out jobs such as pilot, doctor or firefighter through role play. Inside a mall, indoor and safe.
Antique toys from around the world in a historic mansion. For children and for adults seeking nostalgia; a cafe in the garden.
Calligraphy collection and major international exhibitions in a mansion on the Bosphorus. Large garden, chic restaurant, building with elevators.
Contemporary art building with modern architecture; free entry, fully accessible. Dedicated halls for performance and sound installations.
Large seaside park with lawns around the lighthouse. Picnics, dog walking and fishing; flat walking paths.
Quiet neighborhood with colorful wooden houses where a mosque, a church and a synagogue stand side by side. Boutique cafes, a community garden and bookshops; the side streets are sloped.
New 1.2 km waterfront promenade around the cruise port; restaurants, shops and museums. Flat, wide and fully accessible.
Antique and second-hand market held every Sunday in a covered parking lot; records, photographs, furniture. For those who love discovery and bargaining.
